newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - February 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - February 18.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
UNITED FRONT UNFAZED BY CONGRESS DECISION

The ruling United Front (UF) remained apparently unmoved by the Congress party's decision to extend issue-based support only. However, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) hinted at the possibility of moving a no-confidence motion against the government in the budget session of parliament. UF leaders sought to soft-pedal the issue, saying even the earlier unconditional support did not quite mean uncritical support. The BJP, on the other hand, was gearing itself to exploit what it perceived as a clear change of stance on the Congress part. By moving a no-confidence motion, a final decision on which was to be taken, the BJP felt it could put the Congress resoluteness on issue-based support to
Indian Express
APEX COURT ACCEPTS GOVERNMENT'S STATEMENT

The Supreme Court accepted the government's stand that it had not issued any directive to the Central Bureau of Investigations (CBI) which interfered with investigations in any of the politically sensitive cases. The government made clear its position during the on going hawala (illegal money transfers) case proceedings in the apex court. The court asked the CBI to put all offenders in one category without discrimination, to prevent a repeat of the hawala case where attempts were made to protect persons in power.
The Economic Times
CENTRAL BANK CHIEF TO HEAD PANEL ON STATE FINANCE REFORMS

Reserve Bank of India governor C. Rangarajan is likely to head a new commission on state finances which would be set up to go into fiscal reforms at the state level. The Finance Ministry wants Rangarajan to take up the new assignment in view of the serious situation developing in the finances of many states. Sources said once the governor took up the new assignment, he may step down as chief of the central bank.
CELLULAR FIRMS TO REVIEW INVESTMENT PLANS

Foreign companies involved in cellular telecommunication consortiums in India are reviewing their involvement in the industry. This followed the government's decision to hike the charge on calls from fixed line to mobile phones. Though optimistic of the issue being resolved eventually, officials of several foreign companies expressed their disappointment. They added that if the order was not withdrawn or modified, there would be no business case for them to justify their involvement in the privatisation process of telecom in India. The companies contented that this was not part of the tender, and it directly affected 35 to 50 percent of their revenue.
PROFITABLE BANKS MAY EXPAND SANS APPROVAL

Consistently profitable government banks may soon have the freedom to go in for branch expansion and licensing without seeking the central bank's approval. These banks may also be given the freedom to draw up wage agreements with their unions that were independent of the banking industry. At the same time, they would have the option of campus recruitment from leading management institutes. These issues were discussed at a meeting between the chiefs of these banks and the finance minister.
RELIANCE EDGES FOR TOP 10 IN PETROCHEM

Reliance (RIL) would rank among the top ten petrochemical producers globally when its paraxylene and polypropylene plants at Jamnagar, Gujarat, go on stream by 1999. Company sources said RIL had already started work on the Jamnagar site for building capacities for producing 1.4 million tonnes a year of paraxylene and 400,000 tonnes a year of polypropylene. On completion, RIL's total volume output would increase to 9.3 million tonnes a year. RIL would then be the second largest producer of paraxylene and the fifth largest producer of polypropylene worldwide.
Financial Express
BANK PLANS TO FUND TAKEOVERS, EXTEND APPROACH LOANS

Bank of Baroda (BoB) planned to launch schemes for financing takeovers. It would also grant advances to a company which deferred plans to tap the capital market due to adverse market conditions. The BoB board has given in-principle approvals to the twin proposals and only the central bank's clearance was awaited. The bank planned to treat a takeover as a project if a company was willing to tell the reason for it and the impact it would have on its prospects. The other scheme would allow BoB to extend advances to a corporate for undertaking a project for which funds were meant to be raised through a public issue.
CABINET PANEL NOD FOR SETTING UP BROADCASTING AUTHORITY

A cabinet sub-committee approved the setting up of the broadcasting authority for issuing licences to radio and TV companies, including direct to home (DTH) and cable TV firms. It proposed to allow the broadcasting authority to grant licences only to Indian companies. Foreign equity in these companies was capped at 49 percent. The draft also said a person would be allowed to hold licences in only one category of broadcasting and there may be a limit also on the number of such licences. Newspaper proprietors could not hold more than 20 percent equity in a broadcasting company, the draft said.
FOREIGN INVESTORS TOLD TO TEST WATERS

A senior Arthur Andersen executive asked foreign investors to undertake proper feasibility studies before taking the plunge in India. If promoters did not carry the feasibility study in a correct manner, projects might end up with longer gestation periods, he warned. The Arthur Andersen executive cited the example of basic telecommunication projects where the demand analysis was wide off the mark and hence the projects were bound to have longer gestation periods. He also cautioned foreign investors against unrealistic expectations about the pace of implementation.
RELIANCE NYNEX OPT FOR VENDOR FINANCING

The Reliance-Nynex telecommunication joint venture opted for vendor-financing with its two equipment suppliers, Ericsson and Motorola. Corporate banking circles said Ericsson, which would supply switchgears to Reliance-Nynex, has come in with a $40 million financing option with the backing of the Export Credit Agency of Sweden. Motorola, the base-station equipment supplier, volunteered to bring in about $80 million with the backing of the US Exim Bank. The $80 million vendor backing represented a scaledown from the earlier estimate of around $100-110 million, sources said.
Business Standard
RIFT OVER SCOPE OF BILL ON MONEY LAUNDERING

Differences have cropped up between the investigative agencies and the Finance Ministry over the list of economic offences to be covered by the proposed bill against money laundering. The investigative agencies have opposed the ministry's move to keep over-invoicing, under-invoicing and illegal siphoning of funds from public limited companies out of the proposed bill's purview. The panel set up to draft the bill was also divided on whether to fix the responsibility of money laundering transaction on banks. The differences may delay the draft, changed three times already, and preclude tabling of the bill in the budget session of parliament as promised by the finance minister.
STERLING CELLULAR PLANS $175 ADR

The Ruias-controlled Sterling Cellular planned to tap the American depositary receipts (ADR) market with a $175 million issue. Sterling has already received the Finance Ministry's approval for the offering. The company has not yet finalised the lead managers to the issue, sources said. The ADR issue would be the first after the BPL Cellular Holdings' attempt to access the US market failed. BPL's offering had not done well because of the high premium the promoters wanted for the issue.
BRITISH INVESTMENT IN INDIA DECLINES SHARPLY

British investment in India declined sharply despite a number of visits by high-powered business delegations. Available figures indicated investment in India had gone down despite increased investments in many other countries. Indian officials attributed the slowdown in investment to political uncertainties. But British industry invested close to $1 billion in Hong Kong in 1995 despite the prevailing political uncertainty. This was 20 times that of the investment in India.
The Observer
MOODY'S UPGRADES BANK OF INDIA RATING

Moody's Investors Service upgraded its bank financial strength rating for Bank of India (BOI) from E+ to D. Moody's said this was in recognition of the progress made by BOI in implementing new strategies. The changes were reflected in significantly improved financials. BOI's carried forward losses were written off against capital, despite which, capital ratios improved without further injections of government funds. Moody's pointed out that BOI's net non-performing assets were reduced to about seven percent of net loans, one of the best ratios among all the government banks.
TAX REFORM PANEL AGAINST UNIFORM DEPRECIATION

The corporate tax reform panel opposed a uniform mode of depreciation under both Companies and Income Tax Acts. It, however, suggested a reduction in the rate of tax on surcharge from 15 to 10 percent. The panel, set up by the Finance Ministry to make recommendations on corporate tax restructuring, also called for cutting down tax concessions for corporates under the Income Tax Act. Its opposition to a uniform depreciation norms for corporates implied it was not in favour of doing away with the minimum alternate tax.
